findings.title: An update-mode write counts its edge again in the bucket aggregate
findings.intended: CONTEXT.md:173-177 (an upsert replaces the edge); the docstring says aggregates keep the original value.
findings.remedy: Make update subtract the old weight and not count, or rebuild the bucket.
findings.notes: Whole-bucket count 2 and sum 6.0 for one edge of weight 5.0; a window cutting the bucket answers 1; after the delete the bucket counter stays 1. Neither the docstring (original value kept) nor CONTEXT holds.

observed.oracle: whole-bucket count equals the edges at its coordinates (1) and sum their weights

findings.title: A temporal write with no time lands at epoch 0, not at the current time
findings.intended: InsertEdge's own rule: a missing time is now (TemporalIndex.cls:51).
findings.remedy: Send '' for a missing timestamp; stop treating an explicit 0 as missing in BulkInsertCounts.

observed.verdict: single write stored at 0; batch ts 0 stored at 1794609910 (>1767225600)
observed.oracle: a missing time means now on every path; an explicit 0 means 0

findings.title: A temporal write can create node rows that the ledger never records
findings.intended: INV-replay / RPL-B3: with every write made through the ledger, replay equals the store; HD-0501 (assumption): implicitly created endpoints are real effects to record or give derived provenance.
findings.remedy: Per HD-0501: record the endpoint rows a governed temporal op creates, or mark them derived and exclude them from verify.

observed.verdict: verify diverges on node rows the changeset's temporal op created
observed.oracle: with every write made through the ledger, verify() answers equal (RPL-B3, INV-replay)

findings.title: Purges and the row drop delete node rows without the strict-mode check or a record
findings.intended: USER_GUIDE.md:1107-1121 (strict refuses structural writes not made through the ledger); erase_bare_nodes calls the guard (iris_vector_graph/stores/iris_sql_store.py:2823-2825).
findings.remedy: Guard node retirement as erase_bare_nodes is guarded, or skip ledger-known nodes.

observed.verdict: purge deleted governed node rows under strict mode
observed.oracle: strict mode refuses structural deletes not made through the ledger (USER_GUIDE.md:1107-1121)

findings.title: The marker test differs between the deleters and the ledger
findings.intended: ADR-0009 / HD-0302: an explicitly written edge (no JSON-true mark) survives the temporal side; LedgerGenesis treats temporal 1 as an ordinary qualifier (LedgerGenesis.cls:62-75).
findings.notes: An explicit create_edge with qualifiers {"temporal": 1} was deleted by the last temporal delete on its triple (data loss).

observed.verdict: explicit edge with temporal:1 deleted by the temporal delete
observed.oracle: an explicitly written edge (not JSON-true marked) survives the temporal side (ADR-0009)

findings.title: Without the adjacency index, the Python mirror writes an unmarked row for any predicate
findings.intended: ADR-0015 (an opted-out predicate writes nothing else); ADR-0009 (the asserted row is marked).
findings.remedy: Write the marker and honour the opt-out registry, or drop the mirror.
findings.notes: AUDITA declares the adjacency index, so the mirror path is unreachable there (a non-indexed namespace is not available).
findings.observed: create_edge_temporal / bulk_create_edges_temporal insert an unmarked rdf_edges row when not _adjacency_indexed (iris_vector_graph/_engine/temporal.py:309-331, 453-475).

findings.title: TemporalIndex.Purge wipes every graph's temporal index and leaves the marked rows
findings.intended: ADR-0009 amendment: the marked row goes when the triple's last timestamp goes, in every graph; TMP-B9.13.
findings.remedy: Retract marked rows in Purge (or remove it) and fix the create_edge_temporal docstring that advises calling it.
findings.notes: Both graphs' tout gone; both marked rows and ^KG out stay; purge_before afterwards removes 0.

observed.verdict: both graphs' temporal stores wiped; marked rows and adjacency survive every purge
observed.oracle: ADR-0009 amendment: the marked row goes when the triple's last timestamp goes, in every graph

findings.title: The Python structural-row migration cannot read a large graph
findings.intended: The migration backfills every temporal triple of a graph.
findings.remedy: Read with iter_edges_in_window, or call backfill_temporal_structural_rows.
findings.notes: Not run live (36k temporal edges in AUDITA under the shared IRIS lock was not cheap); the cap is the product's own docstring.
findings.observed: _temporal_triples reads with get_edges_in_window(start=0, end=_ALL_TIME_END) (iris_vector_graph/migrations/temporal_structural_rows.py:55-63), whose docstring states a ~35 k-edge cap that raises TemporalWindowError (iris_vector_graph/_engine/temporal.py:500-505).
